title: 111 files of hand-placed work on ac-box that a deploy will delete
description:
The deploy audit found the box's src tree diverges from git by 59 files that have NEVER existed in git on any branch, plus 52 modified ones. Preserved locally as ac-host branch box-state-2026-09-07 (capture only, deliberately unpushed - reviewable via 'git diff main..box-state-2026-09-07').

The largest piece is an entire 'series' racing feature, hand-placed directly on the box outside the pipeline: shared/series_lib.py, bot/series_cmds.py, bot/series_poll*.py, scripts/generate_series_liveries.py, scripts/publish_series_race_pack.py, scripts/kn5_inspect.py, catalog/series/series-1.json, compose/docker-compose.series.yml. bot/bot.py also carries ~5KB of divergence (52136 bytes on box vs 47072 in git).

Confirmed independently: those filenames appear in no commit on any branch, and no last-applied.json exists, so sync_tree's rsync path has never once run for real. The first real run deletes all 59 and reverts bot.py.

DO NOT run the ops pipeline with DOWNTIME=1 until this is reconciled. Reconciliation is a judgement call per file - which belongs in main, which is scratch - so nothing was merged.

Full detail: ac-host/docs/deploy-audit.md.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: Now BLOCKING .27 and, by extension, every future change that lives in the deployed tree rather than the NixOS closure - compose files, sidecar code, content pipeline. last-applied.json still does not exist, so sync_tree has never run once; the first run deletes 59 files. This has moved from 'important finding' to critical path.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text:
RECONCILED and pushed as ac-host c92180f: 74 files, 9403 insertions. The content plane is no longer a destructive operation.

Taken from the box: the series feature and its dependencies (series_lib, skin_livery, skin_uv, kn5, the bot's series commands and polls, livery/race-number generation, race-pack publishing, catalog data, the compose overlay, and the render_cfg/content_manifest changes its tests need).

NOT taken - this was a two-way merge, not a restore. The box is BEHIND git on 11 files, and a wholesale restore would have reverted every fix from today: .gitignore lacks .env.*, flake.nix lacks the monitoring output, modules/arcade-hub.nix is the mojibake copy, modules/ac-host.nix lacks TimeoutStartSec, pending_deploy.py lacks PRESERVE_LOCAL, and the CI compose lacks cgroup_parent. Verified all four still intact after the merge.

Discarded as Windows-copy debris: ZBy4zK7aiLNl5bKp (50 bytes containing a Windows path), the stale top-level arcade-hub.nix, home-arcade's arcade/metadata/crops and docs/plan-arcade.md misfiled in this repo, and src/state/ - owned by an unmappable UID and mounted by nothing, while containers actually bind /var/lib/ac-host/static.

Two defects that bypassing CI had hidden, both fixed: dejavu_fonts was never declared in the flox manifest so five test_skin_livery cases died on a missing font (verified the manifest entry suffices by simulating flox's XDG_DATA_DIRS), and bot/test_bot.py still asserted the unregistered-user copy names /steam-request when it now points at /intake. Full suite green: 95 scripts, 13 bot, 44 sidecar, 20 shared.

title: The arcade tenant exists only on the box and a content deploy will delete it
description:
ac-box's deployed source tree at /var/lib/ac-host/src has FORKED from ac-host git (both at b7b091a). The entire home-arcade integration exists only on the box and was never committed:
  - modules/arcade-hub.nix: not in git at all (plus a stale top-level arcade-hub.nix)
  - flake.nix: 2 lines exposing and composing nixosModules.arcade-hub, not in git
  - hosts/ac-box/configuration.nix: the whole 11-line services.arcade-hub block (enable, lanAddress, gameInterface, rsync, freeciv, mindustry), not in git
  - the box copy also carries 128 CRLF lines, consistent with having been hand-edited from Windows (same provenance as the mojibake in the vendored module)
Drift also runs the OTHER way: the box's modules/ac-host.nix is MISSING 2 lines git has - a TimeoutStartSec = 15min guard with a comment about a sidecar rebuild hanging and blocking boot. So the box is neither ahead nor behind, it is forked.

THE ACTIVE RISK: shared/pending_deploy.py sync_tree() runs 'rsync -a --delete' (falling back to rmtree + copytree). The next Buildkite content deploy therefore DELETES modules/arcade-hub.nix and overwrites flake.nix and configuration.nix with the git versions that never mention arcade-hub. The running system survives until the next nixos-rebuild, at which point freeciv, mindustry, the samba share, rsyncd and the arcade tmpfiles all disappear. Phase 2's cutover IS a nixos-rebuild, so this must be resolved first.

Also invalidates an assumption in the migration plan: phase 1's no-op cannot be validated against git, because git has never described the running system. The reconciliation checklist and any diff must treat the BOX tree as ground truth.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: Resolved. The arcade wiring is now in ac-host git and pushed: canonical module (not the mojibake copy), the two flake lines, and the services.arcade-hub block, all LF. A content deploy can no longer erase the tenant. Note the audit found this was the first of FOUR instances of the same bug class - see .23 for the largest one still open.

title: ci: jobs run in a container again -- the agent's delivery is not the job's sandbox (native.enable = false)
description: Decision 19 Sep 2026: CI jobs are not deployments to the box, so they run in a container. ADR 0009 row 3 moved the buildkite agent native for delivery reasons (one manifest) and dropped, unnamed, the container's second role: the job sandbox (own filesystem incl. /bin/bash, UTC, a checkout that goes with the container, processes that die with a cancelled job). Since the cutover inquire-platform's stack-memory smoke fails only on the native agent (inq-29g: outbox never drained; the same code with the same env passes on WSL on fresh and reused databases). Flip homelab.ci.native.enable back to false (module: compose unit declared exactly as before), record the decision as ADR 0010, and point the cutover runbook's rollback at it. The native minio received cache pushes since the cutover; the compose minio comes back colder unless /var/lib/ci/minio is rsynced into the volume with both stopped (runbook 6) -- acceptable to skip, the cache refills.
notes: homelab#2 merged and switched 19 Sep 01:29-01:33 UTC; operator restarted ac-host-ci by hand (switch does not restart it: shared unit name + restartIfChanged=false). Compose agent + minio up 20:33 CDT. Runbook gap: homelab#3. inq-29g verdict pending on inquire ci-deps-fix build.

title: deploy edge: CI stages the tenant sha, the box checks it out, warms the environment once online, restarts the stub
description: ADR 0009 step 1, the new edge. CI: after wait:~ on main, 'flox push' the environment to FloxHub (owner imkarrer) -- a pushed generation is 'staged' in CONTEXT.md's sense. Box: a systemd path/timer (modeled on modules/deploy) that pulls the generation into /var/lib/agent-hub/env and restarts the stub under the tenant's quiet policy (agent-hub is drainable; assetto's busyCheck is not consulted for it). Decide and record ADR question 1: does activation reach FloxHub at restart time (03:00 dependency on flox.dev, the class of problem homelab-ybm removes for PyPI), or is the pull separate and activation offline from the pinned generation? Record the pushed and applied generation in /var/lib/homelab/ the way pending-closure.json does. bump-lock for agent-hub is removed from ac-host/home-arcade-style triggers once this is live; the flake input stays until the module is gone.
acceptance_criteria: a push to agent-hub main stages a sha on the box and within minutes agent-hub-llm.service is running from /var/lib/agent-hub/env at that sha via flox activate, with no closure switch; the stub's own restart with the network cut works (findings §1); pending/applied environment records exist for hub-status; ADR question 1 answered in docs/flox-findings.md
notes: DECISION 17 Sep (supervisor), from .1/.2 findings: for agent-hub the deploy unit is the TENANT TREE AT A SHA, not a FloxHub generation -- the environment needs llama-swap.yaml and nix/sd-ui.html at run time and a generation carries only manifest+lock, so a checkout is required anyway and FloxHub would be a second copy of one of its files. Shape, mirroring ADR 0006 exactly one layer down: (1) agent-hub's pipeline, on green main, writes /var/lib/homelab/pending-environment-agent-hub.json {sha, tree, queued_at, build} the way queue-closure writes pending-closure.json (the agent has /var/lib/homelab mounted); (2) a path unit on the box (modules/tenant/environment.nix or modules/deploy) runs the pull: git fetch+checkout of the sha into homelab.tenants.agent-hub.environment.dir owned by the tenant user, 'flox activate -d dir -- true' ONCE ONLINE to warm the store and pin GC roots (findings §1), write last-applied-environment-agent-hub.json {sha, run store path of .flox/run, applied_at}, then restart the stub under the tenant's quiet policy (agent-hub is drainable; no busyCheck); (3) hub-status reads the pair. Rollback = stage the previous sha. FloxHub is NOT used for agent-hub; the source of an environment is an option (git sha now; 'floxhub owner/env' is .5's job, where arcade needs nothing from its tree and a generation IS sufficient -- that is where FloxHub push/pull/generations get dogfooded). Turning the stub on (environment.enable = true) is the last commit of this bead, after the pull unit has produced a warmed checkout on the box -- which means this bead's first switch installs the pull unit and stages nothing; the first push to agent-hub main after that is the proof.
close_reason: Live on ac-box 18 Sep 2026. Edge: agent-hub CI trigger -> homelab queue-environment stages sha -> agent-hub-environment-pull.path checks out, substitutes every lock output from MinIO (never compiles), warms once, records, restarts the stub under quiet policy. Proof: 22e85c4 flipped the stub (09:08 CDT, MainPID is llama-swap from /var/lib/agent-hub/env); 942f327 pushed 09:09 -> applied 09:13:14 restarted=[agent-hub-llm.service]. Two on-box findings fixed same morning: dirty-guard on a fresh clone (e02f1c4), un-pushed -dev output compiled (a177338 + plugin a0cea9b). ADR 0009 Accepted.

title: agent-hub: the tenant as a flox environment (manifest, CI gate under the flox plugin, llama-cpp version in the manifest)
description: ADR 0009 step 1, first half. Write agent-hub/.flox/env/manifest.toml: [install] llama-cpp at the version the tenant wants (not the host's 26.05 9190 -- this is the point), the scripts' python, [vars] for the model path and the flags modules/ currently bake into ExecStart. Run it from the manifest on WSL against the fetched model to prove it serves. Gate: agent-hub gets a Buildkite pipeline object (hub/pipelines/agent-hub.json, homelab-luc is the missing hook) and its steps run under the flox plugin like ac-host's. Decide [services] vs a bare command here and record why (ADR question 2). Nothing on the box changes in this bead.
acceptance_criteria: manifest.toml + manifest.lock + env.json tracked; 'flox activate -- llama-server' serves on WSL; agent-hub has a pipeline that goes green under the flox plugin; the choice of services-vs-command is written in the manifest's comments
close_reason: Landed on agent-hub main 6a15c41 (3 commits). Manifest reproduces the live llama-swap + six backends (ik_llama.cpp fork and sd.cpp as flake refs); gate under the flox plugin; build 7 green on the agent with cores=2; closure drvPath unchanged. ADR Q2 answered: flox activate -- <binary>, [services] for the dev shell. Findings in docs/flox-findings.md.

title: homelab: unit stub for a flox tenant, and flox on the box
description: ADR 0009 step 1, second half. modules/platform gets flox at ONE pinned version (the same v1.14.0 hub-gates.sh pins; move the pin to a place both read). agent-hub-llm.service keeps its name, Slice=background.slice, restartIfChanged and hardening, and its ExecStart becomes 'flox activate -d /var/lib/agent-hub/env -- llama-server ...' (or --start-services per the step-1 decision). The contract declaration in hosts/ac-box/tenants.nix is untouched: ports, tier, quiet, state, metrics all still come from there. Prove with the eval harness that the stub lands in the slice and that the drvPath is unchanged with the stub disabled. Secrets: the runner's githubTokenFile via sops -> a [hook] that sources /run/secrets (ADR question 4).
acceptance_criteria: agent-hub-llm.service on the box runs from the flox environment, in background.slice, serving on :8100 with the same flags; docker_name_exporter and the agent-hub scrape job unchanged; flox's version is declared once
notes: Review of .1 (17 Sep), finding 1: manifest hook defaults equal the box's values (AGENT_HUB_THREADS=23, CTX=32768, MODELS=/srv/agent-hub/models, LISTEN, BACKEND_PORT). Either the stub sets all seven AGENT_HUB_* explicitly (and README says defaults are never load-bearing on the box), or drop the box-valued defaults for MODELS/THREADS/CTX so an unset one is llama-swap's hard 'environment variable X is not set' at load. Prefer the second: the stub then cannot silently inherit a stale host fact. Also: the environment needs llama-swap.yaml and nix/sd-ui.html from the tree at run time -- decide checkout-beside-env vs paths passed in.
close_reason: Landed on homelab main 97f0c00 (8 commits, rebased): flox v1.14.0 on the box from the flox flake input (not following nixpkgs, substituted from cache.flox.dev -- new trusted substituter on the platform, nixConfig + --accept-flake-config on the deploy unit and CI); hub-gates reads the pin from flake.lock; homelab.tenants.<n>.environment.{enable,dir,units} additive in schema.nix (config-free), modules/tenant/environment.nix builds the stub, harness eval-environment.nix 7 cases; agent-hub stub declared disabled (drvPath no-op proven). Reviewer 'land after fixes', all four in. ADR Q6 answered for box+dev in findings §6.

title: ADR 0009: tenants become flox environments; the closure keeps the host and the contract
description:
docs/adr/0009-tenants-as-flox-environments.md, proposed 17 Sep 2026. A tenant's contents become a flox environment in its own tree (manifest = dev shell = CI gate = what the box runs); the closure keeps a unit stub per tenant plus the contract (ports, tier, quiet, state, secrets); a flox tenant deploys through FloxHub generations, independently of the closure, so bump-lock stops being how a tenant change reaches the box. L0-L2 stay NixOS. Order by risk: agent-hub, arcade, ci, assetto images (homelab-ybm), observability last or never.

This is dogfooding: the operator works at flox, and each place flox cannot do a job is a product finding, recorded against the ADR's six open questions, not a reason to stop. Every child's handoff answers at least one question.

The ADR moves to Accepted when step 1 has reached the box through the new edge and been watched surviving a restart; docs/architecture.md Part II (L3) and row 24 are updated then.
close_reason: ADR 0009 delivered, 17-19 Sep 2026. Live on ac-box: agent-hub from its environment (sha edge), arcade from FloxHub generation 2, ci native from homelab's own environment, assetto's bot/sidecar images by flox containerize; observability stays NixOS with a written reason (.7). Tenant modules gone from both trees; the box's system derivation unchanged by their leaving (.11). flox 1.16.0 from one rev on the box, the agent, the gate and the workstation (.15). Six questions answered on the box, eleven product asks priced: docs/flox-findings.md. The runner is the workstation's (ws-cb5); the live-generation compare was dropped. Hygiene left to the operator: three FloxHub spike envs, the compose volumes after a green week (runbook §5), the mindustry jar, a reboot.

title: agent-hub builds on push and bumps homelab's lock: pipeline steps, definition, webhook
description: The last unwired edge of the tenant -> box chain (homelab-luc's remaining half, row 24 for this tree). agent-hub had no .buildkite/pipeline.yml and no hub/pipelines definition, so a push created nothing and the lock was bumped by hand. Build: .buildkite/pipeline.yml in agent-hub (its own checks, then trigger homelab with HOMELAB_BUMP_INPUT=agent-hub, the home-arcade shape -- the composition gate is bump-lock's own nix flake check on the bumped lock, before it pushes), hub/pipelines/agent-hub.json in homelab, and one run of hub-pipeline.sh agent-hub to create the object and its webhook. Under ADR 0008 that chain ends in a switch within minutes, not at 03:30; the operator asked for exactly that.

title: observability declares /var/lib/monitoring for backup, but its real state is in /var/lib/grafana and /var/lib/prometheus2
description: Found 14 Sep by the backup implementation (.38): the backup does exactly what the contract says, and the contract is wrong. observability's state.dirs = [/var/lib/monitoring], which now holds only secrets/{grafana-admin,grafana-secret-key,discord-webhook,unpoller.pass} -- 12 K, and all four values are in git since row 23 (.39.3). The state that would actually hurt to lose is /var/lib/grafana (94 M: dashboards, users, annotations) and /var/lib/prometheus2 (70 M: the TSDB), and NO tenant declares either, so hub-backup.sh does not pull them. Fix in hosts/ac-box/tenants.nix: add both to observability's state.dirs (check what the nixpkgs grafana/prometheus modules actually use as their data dir on this box first, incl. any StateDirectory/DynamicUser indirection such as /var/lib/private). Consider whether /var/lib/monitoring should stay declared at all now that its contents are in git. Then re-run hub-backup.sh (adds ~165 M) and confirm the new dirs appear in its output.
acceptance_criteria: hub-backup.sh --list shows the grafana and prometheus dirs; a run pulls them; a restore of a Grafana dashboard file is hash-identical.
close_reason: homelab 5e504e7: observability declares /var/lib/grafana and /var/lib/prometheus2 (state.dirs is inventory-only -- proven by grep of every consumer and an identical stamp-stripped drvPath, so no box side effect); /var/lib/monitoring dropped from the declaration (holds only sops symlinks now). Run under the timer's unit 16 Sep: both pulled with ownership intact, snapshot f770c94a, repo 1.752 GiB; grafana.db restored hash-identical to the staged copy.

title: ADR 0008 decided: the closure switches as soon as it is staged, deferring only while drivers are racing
description: Operator decision 15 Sep 2026, answering the question ADR 0008 left open: arcade's and observability's units may bounce at any hour, so the only thing a switch waits for is people racing. That collapses option 2 -- no dry-activate parsing and no windowOnly policy word are needed, because busyCheck is already the racing gate and the deploy script already defers on it. What is missing is that it only ever runs at 03:30. Build: homelab.deploy.schedule = continuous (a path unit on pending-closure.json plus a short retry timer), a second busy check after the build and immediately before the switch, the build niced so it cannot compete with racing or the model server, and a blackout across the DOWNTIME window so the closure switch and the tenant deploy are not two operators in one room.

title: agent-hub and home-arcade have no build trigger: no webhook, and agent-hub has no pipeline definition
description: Found while fixing homelab-pxk. The push -> build edge on this account is a REPO WEBHOOK, not the Buildkite GitHub App (ac-host proves it; homelab now matches). Neither agent-hub nor home-arcade has one, so a push to either creates no build -- which means bump-lock (homelab-bqo.40) never fires on a tenant push and the lock must be bumped by hand, as it was on 14 Sep for agent-hub be854ca. home-arcade has hub/pipelines/home-arcade.json; agent-hub has NO definition, so hub-pipeline.sh refuses it and whether a Buildkite pipeline exists at all is unknown (the API token lacks read_pipelines). Done when: hub/pipelines/agent-hub.json exists, hub-pipeline.sh ensures both pipelines, both repos carry the webhook the script prints, and a push to each produces a build that triggers homelab's bump-lock.
notes: Half done 14 Sep: hub-pipeline.sh now converges the hook (67b94e8), and running it created home-arcade's. agent-hub still blocked on a decision, not on tooling -- it has no hub/pipelines/agent-hub.json, and writing one means a push to agent-hub becomes a build that triggers bump-lock, i.e. three hops later a system switch. Left for the operator.
close_reason: agent-hub has a pipeline (hub/pipelines/agent-hub.json, .buildkite/pipeline.yml), a webhook (hub-pipeline.sh created it), and the chain is proven: push a988cd6 -> agent-hub/builds/2 green in 6 s -> homelab/builds/14 bump-lock pushed ffd42a3 -> homelab/builds/15 staged it, 55 s end to end. home-arcade's hook created the same way. The hooks are converged by hub-pipeline.sh, not maintained by hand.

title: GitHub pushes stopped creating Buildkite builds after homelab build 7 (14 Sep 13:08 UTC)
description: Five homelab commits pushed 14 Sep 20:27-21:43 UTC (2af84d5..70eb2c8) and agent-hub be854ca produced no build. Buildkite's agents API shows ac-box connected and idle since 13:08 with job: null, so the box is fine and no build was ever created: the push -> build edge (Buildkite GitHub App or repo webhook) stopped delivering. Not readable from WSL (no gh auth; the API token has no read_builds). Check https://github.com/settings/installations (Buildkite -> repository access) and the repos' settings/hooks recent deliveries; until fixed, builds are created by hand with the API (write_builds) as hub-deploy.sh does.
close_reason: homelab had no repo webhook and the Buildkite GitHub App did not cover it, so a push never created a build; ac-host (the one tree that built on push) does it through a repo webhook, not the App. Added the same hook to homelab (push + pull_request, json, the URL hub-pipeline.sh prints). Proven 14 Sep 23:34 UTC: push -> GitHub delivery 200 -> build 9 started 2 s later, green, staged 0123c54. Still open elsewhere: agent-hub and home-arcade have no hook either, and agent-hub has no hub/pipelines definition at all -- see the follow-up bead.

title: CI agent: Nix builds unsandboxed, and a Go build's telemetry creates /homeless-shelter, failing every homelab flake check
description: Found 14 Sep on homelab builds 2 and 3, the first ever on the homelab pipeline (cluster move done, .41/.50). `nix flake check -L` evaluates fine, then 'running 6 flake checks' dies: error: home directory '/homeless-shelter' exists; please remove it to assure purity of builds without sandboxing. The agent container runs Nix with sandbox off (no CAP_SYS_ADMIN; build-users-group empty, builds as root); a Go package that is not in any cache gets BUILT during the checks (new with sops-nix in the closure -- sops-install-secrets is Go), Go 1.25's telemetry writes /homeless-shelter/.config/go/telemetry, and Nix refuses every subsequent unsandboxed build. Cleared by hand between builds 2 and 3; build 3 recreated it in 28 s. ac-host's own pipeline never trips this because it evaluates without building. Fix in ac-host compose/docker-compose.buildkite.yml, agent service: run the Nix sandbox -- privileged: true (the container already mounts /var/run/docker.sock, so it is root-equivalent on the host and this widens nothing; say so in the comment) or the narrowest working set (cap_add SYS_ADMIN + security_opt seccomp:unconfined + apparmor:unconfined) if that is proven to work; and set sandbox = true for Nix in the container -- the image's /etc/nix/nix.conf comes from the flox-buildkite-plugin image, so pass NIX_CONFIG: 'sandbox = true' in the service environment (nix merges it) unless a cleaner hook exists. Verify the sandbox actually engages: a job running `nix build --expr 'derivation ...'` or simply the homelab flake check succeeding. Reaches the box via the DOWNTIME build's tree sync + ac-host-ci recreate (HAZARD 2: the restart is from ssh or the 04:00 timer, never from a job).
acceptance_criteria: ac-host gate PASS; after the tree applies and ac-host-ci recreates, a homelab build's flake-check job passes and queue-closure writes /var/lib/homelab/pending-closure.json.
close_reason: ac-host 069c060 + f5cd928: sandbox = true, sandbox-fallback = false, privileged (only thing that engages the sandbox on ac-box; decided by the operator). Build 7's flake check passed sandboxed in 24 min, compiling ik_llama.cpp.

title: ac-host: trust the flox-binary-cache-2 public key alongside -1, and let minio-init rewrite the cache user's secret on every start
description: Coupled to homelab bead .39.1 (5adba64): the Nix cache signing key rotates to flox-binary-cache-2 (private half in sops, rendered into the CI env). The agent image bakes S3_CACHE_PUBLIC_KEY into /etc/nix/nix.conf extra-trusted-public-keys from compose/docker-compose.buildkite.yml line 92 (bake arg) and line 133 (agent env default); the same -1 value is repeated in .buildkite/pipeline.yml:13, ops.yml:15, series.yml:12, .buildkite/flox-binary-cache.pub, compose/env.buildkite.example:27, docs/ci-cd.md, and home-arcade .buildkite/pipeline.yml:11 (s3-cache-public-key). Add, space-separated after -1, everywhere (keep -1 so the warm cache stays valid): flox-binary-cache-2:ESa71iIsMeX6Wu7EBiXXZlJraWI0HF4xdOF/ivG4UTo=  (home-arcade is another tree: separate follow-up, note it). Also compose/minio-init.sh: drop the 'mc admin user info' guard so 'mc admin user add' runs every start -- the server's CreateUser rewrites an existing user's secret (MinIO RELEASE.2025-09-07), which makes an access-key rotation just a new env value plus a bounce. Until the tenant tree carrying this is applied (DOWNTIME build) the agent trusts only -1 and the cache user has the old secret: pushes to the cache fail auth and new paths signed -2 are untrusted; jobs still run. Minutes to hours, cache only.
acceptance_criteria: ac-host gate PASS; grep for flox-binary-cache-1 shows -2 beside it at every hit; minio-init.sh has no existence guard; docs/ci-cd.md says a rotation is: new value in homelab sops, switch, bounce ac-host-ci.

title: ci: .env.buildkite from a sops template, with the cluster agent token and rotated cache keys
description: The ci tenant's env file (/var/lib/ac-host/src/compose/.env.buildkite, root 0600, gitignored, hand-placed) becomes sops.templates.ci-env rendered at sops-nix's default path, and homelab.ci.envFile points at it (the option exists: modules/ci/default.nix ~line 188); no copy unit -- nothing inside a container opens this file, systemd EnvironmentFile= and compose --env-file both read it on the host, and it stops living inside the tenant tree ci_downtime.py syncs. Secrets in it: BUILDKITE_AGENT_TOKEN (now the CLUSTER token, sops key buildkite-agent-token, 482de9f7 -- this is what moves the agent into the Default cluster), MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD, S3_CACHE_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, S3_CACHE_SIGNING_KEY, GITHUB_STATUS_TOKEN (same value as assetto's github-status-token already in sops), plus non-secret config. The two S3_CACHE_* values were exposed in an agent transcript on 14 Sep: generate NEW ones rather than migrating the old (they are MinIO-local; the signing key is a Nix cache key pair -- check how minio-init / the cache expects them and regenerate the pair the same way). Agent tags must keep queue=self; BUILDKITE_AGENT_NAME stays ac-box.
acceptance_criteria: secrets.nix renders ci-env; homelab.ci.envFile = the rendered path; all secret keys present in secrets/ac-box.yaml; homelab gate PASS and the sops manifest builds; on switch + ac-host-ci bounce the agent reconnects in the Default cluster (GET /v2/organizations/isaac-karrer/agents shows cluster non-null, queue self).

title: drivers_online: busyCheck fails OPEN on a non-HTTP answer, and its test flakes on TCP self-connect
description: Found 13 Sep gating wt/homelab-bqo.49: scripts/test_drivers_online.py::test_empty_lobbies_are_not_busy errors roughly 1 run in 8 with 'http.client.BadStatusLine: GET /api/details HTTP/1.1' -- the client read back its own request line. Cause: the test binds two _Lobby servers on random ephemeral ports and _run_against() makes main() probe every port between them; when the kernel picks a source port equal to the probed port, Linux completes a TCP self-connect and urlopen reads its own bytes. Two defects. title: Slicing a compose unit does NOT fence its containers
description:
Invalidates the premise of .12 and the modules/ci draft (.19), found while verifying phase 6.

Docker container cgroup placement is decided by dockerd, NOT by the cgroup of whoever invoked docker. Proof: the CI containers were started by a human from an SSH session, which lives in user.slice, yet they sit in system.slice/docker-<id>.scope. Container scopes are siblings of the invoking unit, not children of its slice.

So wrapping the CI stack in a systemd unit and assigning THAT unit to batch.slice would not fence anything. Verified the agent's effective cpuset is 0-55 - fully unfenced, free to take the cores races run on. Also verified: daemon.json sets no cgroup-parent (so dockerd defaults to system.slice), no container sets CgroupParent or CpusetCpus, and no compose file has cgroup_parent, cpuset, cpu_shares or cpus fields.

This means the tiering guarantee currently protects against arcade and agent-hub but NOT against CI, which is the single workload most likely to consume all 56 threads.

Real options, none of which is 'add a systemd unit':
  1. compose 'cgroup_parent: batch.slice' per service - containers land inside the slice and inherit AllowedCPUs.
  2. compose 'cpuset: 28-55' per service - direct, but duplicates the fence rather than deriving it from the tier.
  3. dockerd --cgroup-parent default - fences EVERY container including the race servers, so almost certainly wrong here.
Option 1 is the one that composes with the tier model, since the slice already carries the derived limits. The modules/ci draft needs reworking around it before adoption, and .19's design note should be corrected rather than followed.
close_reason: Closed

Proved on ac-box (systemd cgroup driver, cgroup v2) that --cgroup-parent=batch.slice yields cpuset 28-55 while no parent yields 0-55, then set cgroup_parent: batch.slice on all three CI compose services in ac-host 4581df4. homelab now warns when any needsDocker tenant sits in a fenced tier (fires for ci, correctly silent for assetto since critical is unfenced by design), and ADR 0005 records the mechanism plus the two rejected alternatives (per-service cpuset duplicates what the tier derives; dockerd --cgroup-parent would fence the race servers too).

The resolution is that critical tenants never need to be in a slice at all: the protection comes from AllowedCPUs fencing background and batch AWAY from the low cores, not from confining races. comments.text:
PREMISE CORRECTED. This ticket (and my earlier reports) said rootless Docker on ac-box forced --network host. The WSL2 dev box is the rootless one. The claim came from run-task.sh's own comment, written about the dev box, which I carried forward without checking.

title: agent-hub: a code reviewer from a different model family beside coder -- trial gpt-oss-120b
description:
Why: bead-loop's rule is that every claim is checked by something that is not the model that made it, but stage 2 is acbox/coder implementing with acbox/instruct reviewing -- same Qwen3-Next base, same blind spots. The 20 Sep 2026 memory audit says the box holds coder (96 GiB RSS) + instruct (80 GiB) with ~68 GiB spare, ~110 GiB once the image models are gone (homelab-b9u). A third resident model of a different lineage, used only as the review call, is what that RAM is for.

Constraint set for this CPU box (dual E5-2680 v4, no GPU, ik_llama.cpp 3bb386e): decode is bandwidth-bound, so active parameters are the budget -- <= ~6B active for >= 7 tok/s; total size must fit beside coder (<= ~110 GiB after b9u) or replace instruct; the architecture must be in ik's support list (README, checked 20 Sep: gpt-oss/MXFP4 yes, GLM-4.5/Air yes, Qwen3-Next yes; MiniMax-M2, Nemotron-3, Mellum2 not listed -- Mellum2's GGUFs need an experimental llama.cpp build); must do tool calls through --jinja (the reviewer reads files); must run under -rtr (verify repack of MXFP4 tensors, or run this one backend without -rtr).

Candidates, in order: (1) gpt-oss-120b, 117B-A5.1B, native MXFP4 ~63 GB, Apache-2.0, OpenAI lineage; fits beside coder AND instruct; expected ~7-8 tok/s by active-param ratio; reasoning effort settable per request (low/medium for reviews). (2) GLM-4.5-Air or newer -Air, 106B-A12B, Q4_K_M ~60 GB / Q8 ~110 GB; Zhipu lineage, strong agentic-coding; ~3-4 tok/s at 12B active -- slower, second choice. Not: dense 24B+ (Devstral etc., ~3 tok/s), 235B+ MoE (fits only alone).

Steps: fetch the GGUF to /srv/agent-hub/models (scripts/fetch-model.sh entry); bench with scripts/bench/bench.sh on the box inside background.slice (pp1024, tg32, -rtr on/off) before touching the table; add a 'reviewer' entry to llama-swap.yaml (one slot, ctx 32768, own --cache-ram) and to matrix set0; homelab configuration.nix description + resident-set arithmetic; then run 5 real bead reviews through it side by side with acbox/instruct on the same diffs (bead-loop logs keep both) and decide by rejection quality, not benchmarks. bead-loop's config follows in its own bead.
acceptance_criteria: The chosen model is resident with coder and instruct (/running shows four backends incl. embed); a lone review runs >= 7 tok/s by the review log's step timestamps; five reviews compared against acbox/instruct on the same diffs, verdicts recorded in this bead's notes; llama-swap.yaml comment names the model, the quant, the measured pp/tg, and why it was chosen over the runner-up.

title: Convert the other eight leaderboard.json writers to atomic_json
description:

The judgement per call site is what to do when read_json raises - skip the update like publish_health does, or fail loudly - and that depends on whether the caller is mirroring derived state or is the authoritative writer of it.

Not attempted alongside the acctl fix deliberately: eight call sites in five files across three services is a bigger blast radius than the one bug that was actively destroying data every boot.

Once enforce.firewall provides interface-scoped equivalents, the globals become redundant AND harmful: they are what would expose AC's HTTP and Grafana on eno1 the moment the dual-NIC plan brings it up.

That keeps the module correct used standalone rather than depending on a consumer to re-declare its ports, and it is a narrowing rather than a deletion of protection.

title: acctl publish_health races sidecar on leaderboard.json
description: acctl.py::publish_health() does a non-atomic, unlocked read-modify-write of leaderboard.json that races against sidecar/plugin.py's atomic writes, and silently persists an EMPTY board if the read ever hits corrupt JSON. It runs on every boot via up-static, so the window recurs. Needs a design decision (lock, atomic write, or single-writer) rather than a quick patch. From ac-host/docs/deploy-audit.md.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text:
FIXED in ac-host fd075ed, and wider than described. publish_health fell back to {} on any read error then wrote that back, so one transient read failure permanently erased every driver's standings - on a path that runs at every boot via up-static. The plain write_text was also truncate-then-write, which is itself how a reader gets the unparseable JSON that triggers the erase, so the two defects fed each other.

Also: NINE files write leaderboard.json (acctl, ci_publish_pages, seed_github_env, series_lib, plugin, push_status, bot, server_health) and nothing in the repo used os.replace or any lock. It was not a two-writer race, it was a nine-writer truncate-and-hope.

New shared/atomic_json.py: read_json distinguishes absent (None) from unreadable (raises), so corruption can never be silently treated as start-fresh; write_json uses a temp file in the destination dir plus fsync and os.replace. publish_health now warns and skips the mirror when the board is unreadable - the health flag is persisted separately by write_flag/clear_flag, so the worst case is a stale indicator rather than lost standings.

9 tests including that a failed write leaves the previous standings intact and no temp files behind.

title: sync_tree has no backup or rollback despite _local_wipe_backup implying one
description: _local_wipe_backup/ appears in RSYNC_EXCLUDES but is a ghost: no code in the repo or on the box creates, reads or restores from it. sync_tree() therefore has no backup or rollback capability at all, despite the naming implying one should exist. Given it runs rsync -a --delete against a tree that has repeatedly turned out to hold un-backed-up state, a pre-sync snapshot would have prevented all four instances of the bug class found today.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text:
DONE, ac-host. sync_tree now takes a pre-sync snapshot via rsync's own --backup/--backup-dir, so anything deleted or overwritten is moved aside rather than destroyed. Snapshots live at <state>/_local_wipe_backup/<timestamp>, a sibling of the synced tree (never inside it, or rsync recurses into its own backups), pruned to the newest five, and a no-change sync leaves none behind.

Two bugs found by testing rather than reasoning: the snapshot root was derived from state_dir() which defaults to a hardcoded /var/lib/ac-host, so every existing caller - which passes only (src, dest) - failed immediately; it now derives from dest.parent. And utcnow() is second-resolution, so two syncs in the same second shared a directory, defeating both the one-snapshot-per-sync model and the empty-snapshot cleanup.

Also worth recording: my first overwrite test proved nothing. Both files were 3 bytes written in the same second, and rsync's quick-check is size+mtime, so it skipped the transfer and never attempted a backup. The test now uses a different size and a backdated mtime.

5 regression tests added. Full suite green: 25 shared, 95 scripts, 13 bot, 44 sidecar.

title: Freeciv's real UDP port is 4555 on 0.0.0.0, not the declared 5556

So the UDP rule the module writes protects a port nothing listens on, and the port freeciv actually uses is bound to all interfaces and covered only by default-deny. Not currently exploitable (nothing forwards it), but the module's stated intent and the runtime disagree. Decide whether 4555 is needed at all (it is freeciv's LAN announce) and either declare it properly or bind freeciv's UDP to the LAN address.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: Fixed in home-arcade 34906cb and gated. freeciv-server binds TCP 5556 to lanAddress but its UDP socket is 4555 on 0.0.0.0 - the LAN-announce/discovery port, not the game port. The module was opening UDP 5556 where nothing listens while the real port went undeclared. Added a freeciv.announcePort option (default 4555) rather than deriving it, because --bind governs only the game socket so the announce socket stays on 0.0.0.0 and interface scoping is the only control available. Also registered 4555 in the port registry and narrowed 5556 to tcp-only.

title: agent-hub: a small resident utility model for cheap calls -- titles, summaries, pre-checks, reranking
description:
Why: every cheap call today either lands on an 80B slot (opencode's small_model, title generation, summaries) or on the WSL box's GPU. A 4-8B model resident on ac-box costs 4-13 GiB of the RAM freed by homelab-b9u and answers those in seconds, keeping the 80Bs' two slots for reviews and sessions.

Candidates: (1) Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-Q8_0.gguf -- ALREADY on the box (/srv/agent-hub/models, 4 GB, kept back from the b9u purge for this); zero download, Qwen3 arch, ~40+ tok/s expected. (2) gpt-oss-20b, 21B-A3.6B, MXFP4 ~13 GB -- different family, so it could also front a cheap 'is this diff trivially fine / does it touch only the named files' pre-check before the 80B review, in the spirit of homelab-e00. (3) Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B beside the embedder for Qdrant retrieval, if inquire-platform's retrieval wants it -- separate decision, same bead only if trivial.

Steps: llama-swap.yaml entry 'utility' (one slot, ctx 16384, small --cache-ram, 8 threads not 23 -- a 4B at 23 threads starves the 80B's prefill for no gain; measure), add to matrix set0; homelab description + resident arithmetic; opencode's acbox provider gets the model, and small_model in ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json points at it (bead-loop side bead covers that). Measure tg and pp with bench.sh first; record in the yaml comment.
acceptance_criteria: utility is resident with the 80Bs (/running); a 200-token title/summary call returns in < 5 s while a review is running on coder; the yaml comment carries the measured numbers and the thread-count decision.

title: hub-*.sh resolve HUB from $BASH_SOURCE without readlink -f
description: All seven scripts/hub-*.sh set HUB=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.."). Reached through a symlink on PATH, dirname resolves the LINK's directory, so HUB becomes ~/.local and hub/repos.psv is not found: every repo name reads as unknown and hub-gates exits without gating anything. hub-evals.sh is fixed (readlink -f); the other six are not, so only hub-evals is safe to symlink today. Fix is the same one-liner in each.
acceptance_criteria: each hub-*.sh works when invoked through a symlink on PATH; all are linked into ~/.local/bin

title: Index the four trees, ADRs and beads into Qdrant through the embedding model
description: Follow-up to homelab-67n: a chunker/indexer that embeds the docs, ADRs, CONTEXT.md, skills and bead text of the four trees into the Qdrant collection, re-run on change, and a search tool the inspector and local worker can call instead of grepping whole trees into the 32k context.
close_reason: scripts/hub-index.sh and scripts/hub-search.sh. 854 points: the tracked .md/.nix/.sh/.py/.yml/.psv of the four trees in 80-line, 12k-char overlapping chunks (the char cap is what keeps architecture.md's long table rows inside the 8k context) plus one point per bead. Deterministic ids, a content sha per chunk so a re-run only embeds what changed (full re-run 8 s; first embed 9 min at 680 tok/s), and a per-tree stale delete. Search prints tree/path:lines with a snippet; --json for tools; -t restricts to one tree or the beads. The inspector and local worker are pointed at it. Embed model went from 4 to 23 threads (65ce6cc) -- the 4.8x that made the first run affordable.

title: The box builds the closure twice: its own store at switch time, and again inside the CI agent's separate /nix volume

The agent's /nix is the named volume ac-host-ci_buildkite-nix; the only cache it shares with anything is MinIO, and only CI pushes there. Options: (a) after every switch, the box pushes its system closure to the MinIO cache (nix copy --to s3://flox-binary-cache..., signed with the same key -- the private key is in sops now) so the agent substitutes what the box built; (b) nix-serve / ssh-ng substituter from the host store into the agent (loopback); (c) accept the one-time cost per new derivation. (a) is small and also warms the cache for the next box switch.
acceptance_criteria: a homelab build after a box switch does not rebuild a package the host store already has.
